In /opt/nxeon-staging, the user wants one-click game type installs for their Minecraft servers — presets like Skyblock, Prison, Factions, KitPvP, etc.

Read these files first:
- `components/customer/gamepanel/GameServerPanel.tsx` — tab container
- `components/customer/gamepanel/types.ts` — PanelTab type
- `lib/actions-game-control.ts` — existing server actions (see sendGameCommand, the RCON pattern)
- `lib/game-config.ts` — game configuration schema

Build a "Game Modes" feature:

1. Create `components/customer/gamepanel/GameModePresets.tsx`:
   - A grid of preset cards, each representing a popular Minecraft game type
   - Presets to include (at minimum): Survival (default), Creative, Skyblock, Prison, Factions, KitPvP, Hunger Games / UHC, Parkour, Bedwars, Anarchy/2b2t-style
   - Each card shows: name, short description, an icon/emoji, and a "Setup" button
   - Clicking "Setup" should show a confirmation dialog explaining what will change
   - The actual setup applies game rules + server.properties changes via existing RCON commands + the `updateGameSetting` action (or direct RCON). For example:
     - Skyblock: sets gamemode survival, keepInventory true, pvp false, spawnRadius 0
     - Prison: gamemode adventure, pvp false, keepInventory true
     - Creative: gamemode creative, doDaylightCycle false, doMobSpawning false
     - KitPvP: gamemode survival, keepInventory true, pvp true, naturalRegeneration true
     - Anarchy: gamemode survival, pvp true, keepInventory false, difficulty hard
   - After applying, show a success message with what was changed
   - Add a note: "This changes game rules and server settings. It does NOT install plugins — install plugins from the Plugins tab for the full experience."

2. Create a server action in `lib/actions-game-control.ts`:
   - `applyGameModePreset(serverId: string, presetId: string)` 
   - Each preset defines a list of RCON commands to run + server.properties changes
   - Uses existing `mcRcon` helper for RCON commands
   - Returns success/failure with details of what was applied

3. DO NOT add this as a new tab. Instead, this should be rendered inside the Settings tab area of the server page (`app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx`). Find where `GameSettings` or settingsPanel is rendered, and add `GameModePresets` below or above the existing settings for Minecraft servers. Look for where settings are assembled to understand the pattern.

Run `npx tsc --noEmit` when done. Use Nxeon dark theme styling.

718	/**

720	 * keys are dropped; missing keys fall back to the field default. Returns a clean,
721	 * fully-populated values object ready to persist to `Server.gameConfig`.
722	 */
723	export function validateConfig(
724	  family: string,
725	  values: Record<string, unknown> | null | undefined
726	): ValidateResult {
727	  const schema = GAME_CONFIG_SCHEMAS[family];
728	  if (!schema) return { ok: false, error: `Unknown game family "${family}".` };
729	
730	  const input = values ?? {};
731	  const out: Record<string, string | number | boolean> = {};
732	
733	  for (const field of schema.fields) {
734	    const raw = input[field.key];
735	    const provided = raw !== undefined && raw !== null;
736	
737	    switch (field.type) {
738	      case "bool": {
739	        out[field.key] = provided ? raw === true || raw === "true" || raw === "on" : (field.default as boolean);
740	        break;
741	      }
742	      case "int": {
743	        let n = provided ? Number(raw) : (field.default as number);
744	        if (!Number.isFinite(n)) return { ok: false, error: `${field.label} must be a number.` };
745	        n = Math.trunc(n);
746	        if (field.min !== undefined && n < field.min)
747	          return { ok: false, error: `${field.label} must be at least ${field.min}.` };
748	        if (field.max !== undefined && n > field.max)
749	          return { ok: false, error: `${field.label} must be at most ${field.max}.` };
750	        out[field.key] = n;
751	        break;
752	      }
753	      case "enum": {
754	        const v = provided ? String(raw) : String(field.default);
755	        if (!field.options?.some((o) => o.value === v))
756	          return { ok: false, error: `Invalid value for ${field.label}.` };
757	        out[field.key] = v;
758	        break;
759	      }
760	      case "string": {
761	        const v = provided ? String(raw) : String(field.default);
762	        if (v.length > 256) return { ok: false, error: `${field.label} is too long (max 256 chars).` };
763	        // CONFIG INJECTION: these values are written verbatim into LINE-ORIENTED
764	        // files on the customer's VM by worker/game-config.ts —
765	        // `server.properties` (`motd=<value>`), Rust's `server.cfg`
766	        // (`server.hostname "<value>"`) and Valheim's launch-args file. A newline
767	        // therefore does not set one option, it appends arbitrary further
768	        // options: a motd of "hi\nenable-rcon=true\nrcon.password=x" turns RCON
769	        // on with a chosen password, and that password is then read back out of
770	        // the same file and interpolated into an `mcrcon` command line.
771	        // `enum`/`int`/`bool` are constrained by their own branches; `string` was
772	        // the only field type with no allowlist at all, so it is checked here —
773	        // at the one point every caller (UI, server action and worker re-validation)
774	        // already goes through.
775	        // eslint-disable-next-line no-control-regex
776	        if (/[\x00-\x1f\x7f]/.test(v)) {
777	          return {
778	            ok: false,
779	            error: `${field.label} may not contain line breaks or control characters.`,
780	          };
781	        }
782	        out[field.key] = v;
783	        break;
784	      }
785	    }
786	  }
787	
788	  return { ok: true, values: out };
